issue.title: Is `NULL` allowed to be expanded to an extension?

discussion.p:
In some current implementations (e.g., in GCC and Clang's own <stddef.h> header), the `NULL` macro may be expanded to the `__null` extension (demo). Although `__null` can be used interchangeably with zero-value integer literals of the same type in most contexts, its exact spelling is observable.
LWG requires `NULL` to be expanded to a literal, and a pedantic reading may suggest that only standard literals are permitted. In other words, if a program requires `NULL` to be expanded as a standard literal (in either compile time or runtime), LWG seemingly requires implementations to support it, which in turns renders the existing use of the `__null` extension non-conforming.
